auditMatching.authorization: dispatch.py writes a tool row with outcome success only after authentication, the key grant check, and the store ownership check pass, and the upstream call returns without is_error. A failed authorization writes outcome unauthorized instead.
auditMatching.upstreamExecution: upstream_id and duration_ms are set only on rows written after the registry call to the store upstream returns.
auditMatching.timestampSemantics: occurred_at is written after the upstream call completes, so row 50 (Store C) precedes row 51 (Store B) by completion order, not by issue order.
auditMatching.orderFieldsNotInAudit: By design, audit rows hold no arguments or results. Order IDs, statuses, totals, and currencies are matched against the MCP responses and the store databases, not the audit log.

limitations: Audit rows and gateway access logs carry no client identity or user agent, and all traffic arrives from 127.0.0.1 through the port-forward. Attribution of rows 50 and 51 to the Cursor MCP client rests on: actor d81bf7a2acd3750f; timing that matches the agent's two parallel CallDynamicTool calls; matching results; and no terminal transcript showing another client calling the gateway in that window.

The token in /home/naval/.cursor/mcp.json was not compared to the key record (no hashing or value read). Its identity is inferred because Cursor's authenticated calls resolved to actor d81bf7a2acd3750f and the project config cannot supply a token.

The raw key also remains as an exported variable in the owner's terminal shell pid 374685. This file does not establish how the owner first obtained the raw key beyond audit row 45 (admin:issue_key by 169d3b25942f065b).

secretScan.sixteenCharacterOverlap: One 16-character substring of the stored token appears in this file. Gateway tokens have the form urk_<16-hex key id>.<token_urlsafe(32) secret> (apps/gateway/app/keys.py generate_key), 64 characters in total, which matches the stored literal's length. The key id is public and recorded here by design. A follow-up check to confirm the overlap is exactly the key id was not run, because it would read the raw token again.
